name: Human exact-form law
tagline: Per-benchmark literature-derived parametric scaling laws (Tao vocab, SLDBench Expert-B lr/bsz, Muennighoff data-constrained); fit by per-group nonlinear least squares.
formula: $$ \begin{aligned} L_{\text{vocab}} &= E + A N^{-\alpha} + B V^{-\beta} + C D^{-\gamma} \\ L_{\text{lrbsz}} &= A D^{-\alpha} + B N^{-\beta} + C + K_l (l - l_0)^2 + E\,(\log b + b_0/b) \\ L_{\text{dc}} &= E + A N^{-\alpha} + B D_{\text{eff}}^{-\beta},\quad D_{\text{eff}} = U(1 - e^{-D/U}) \end{aligned} $$

nodes.label: Train trials grouped by categorical metadata
Eval on held-out trials per group

diff_from_baseline: Tao et al. 2024 (vocabulary scaling); SLDBench paper arXiv:2507.21184 (Expert-B law, App. A.4); Muennighoff et al. 2023 (data-constrained). Symbolic Chinchilla-style laws fit per categorical group via multi-start nonlinear least squares; the lrbsz fit also seeds from the paper's reference coefficients.

name: Kernel ridge
tagline: Black-box RBF kernel-ridge baseline on raw + log-transformed numerics and one-hot categoricals.
diff_from_baseline: Saunders, Gammerman & Vovk 1998 (kernel ridge regression). Generic RBF kernel ridge on standardized + log-encoded mixed numeric/categorical features; intentionally non-parametric to gauge how much symbolic structure helps over a black-box predictor.

name: SLDAgent-style symbolic
tagline: Discovered-style symbolic forms with cross-axis interactions: V*D cross term, (lr,bsz) correlated quadratic bowl, multiplicative repeat-efficiency on D_eff.
formula: $$ \begin{aligned} L_{\text{vocab}} &= E + A\,N^{-a_1}V^{-a_2}D^{-a_3} + A_{vd}V^{-g_1}D^{-g_2} \\ L_{\text{lrbsz}} &= L_{\text{Chinchilla}}(N,D) + k\big(dx^2+dy^2+2\rho\,dx\,dy\big) \\ L_{\text{dc}} &= E + A N^{-\alpha} + B (D\cdot \eta)^{-\beta},\; \eta = (1+D/(UR))^{-1} \end{aligned} $$
diff_from_baseline: SLDAgent-style stand-in baseline. Reasonable surrogate symbolic forms in the SLDAgent spirit (cross-axis interactions, correlated quadratic bowls, repeat-efficiency multipliers) since the agent's exact discovered formulas are not published.

name: XGBoost
tagline: Gradient-boosted regression trees on engineered (raw + log) numerics and one-hot categoricals; trained in log-target space when targets are positive.
pseudocode:
1. Encode numerics as (standardized raw) $\oplus$ (standardized $\log(1+x)$); one-hot encode categoricals
2. If $\min y > 0$, set target $\leftarrow \log y$ (use_log = True), else keep $y$
3. Fit XGBRegressor: $n\_\text{estimators}=120$, $\max\_\text{depth}=3$, $\eta=0.05$, subsample=0.9, colsample=0.8, $\lambda=1.0$, tree_method='hist'
4. Fall back to sklearn GradientBoostingRegressor if XGBoost unavailable
5. Predict on test, exponentiate if use_log
diff_from_baseline: Chen & Guestrin 2016 (XGBoost, KDD). Off-the-shelf gradient-boosted trees baseline on engineered features, trained in log-target space when targets are strictly positive.
